sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Barbarea vulgaris is a biennial or short-lived perennial of the mustard family, native from Europe to Japan and introduced in North America. It forms a basal rosette, then erect flowering stems with yellow four-petalled flowers and narrow siliques. It is common in damp ground, ditches, river margins and hedgerows.

sections.title: Food and caution
sections.text: Some references report young leaves eaten raw or cooked, but extension guidance also notes low-severity poisonous characteristics and possible kidney effects. The plate's rosette, yellow flowers and siliques fit the species; the food report is not a recommendation to eat it.
